title: Seamless artifact intake, multi-format conversion, and compatibility gate for open-model onboarding
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Goal: Deliver an end-to-end intake pipeline that accepts community weights in multiple common formats, deterministically converts them to Redwood runtime artifacts, performs compatibility and quality validation, and publishes a signed performance profile and recommended pin. This ticket implements the conversion worker, deterministic validation gate, automated profiling harness, and the compatibility policy enforcement points that block publishing when checks fail. The pipeline must support: 1) streaming weight uploads (S3/HF hub links), 2) conversion to runtime formats (quantization-aware flows: fp16, int8/4 where available, fused-kernel friendly layouts), 3) deterministic checksum and shape validation, 4) behavioral smoke tests (token-level equivalence within tolerance), 5) resource footprint estimation and profiling (latency p50/p95, memory, kv-cache overhead), 6) artifact signing (sigstore) and metadata publish (model pin + compatibility matrix + performance profile). This work ties into the artifact gateway, admission permissioning, and the pinflow orchestrator. We must minimize manual review while retaining a clear canary/publish path for higher-risk models.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline accepts weights via S3 URL, HF repo reference, or direct upload and persists a source artifact with provenance metadata
Conversion worker produces runtime artifact(s) for supported targets (torch->runtime FP16, optional quantized variants) and emits deterministic checksums
Compatibility gate runs automated shape/checksum, token-level smoke tests against a canonical prompt set, and flags regressions when outputs diverge beyond configured tolerances
Profiling job records p50/p95 latency for baseline sequences (8, 64, 512 tokens), peak memory, and kv-cache behavior; profile is saved and associated with the model artifact
Artifact signing via sigstore is performed for published pins and metadata contains the signing certificate thumbprint
Publish step writes a model pin, compatibility matrix, and performance profile to the model catalog only when all gates pass; failures generate actionable errors and link to logs
Operator can trigger a manual canary rollout of new pin to Dedicated test pool and observe metrics; rollback mechanism reverts pin in the catalog and invalidates canary assignments
testing_plan: Unit tests for conversion worker with golden weights (small Llama-like toy model) to verify bit-exact deterministic conversion when no quantization is applied
Integration tests: ingest -> convert -> smoke validate -> profile -> publish in CI using ephemeral S3 bucket and mocked runtime to validate flow and metadata wiring
Performance regression tests: compare new profile against historical baselines with configurable tolerance thresholds (default 20% p95), surface alerts in CI
Chaos test: simulate partial worker failure and ensure pipeline marks artifact as 'ingest-failed' and no publish occurs
Security test: verify sigstore signing key rotation path and that unsigned artifacts are rejected by publish gate
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal canary only. Enable pipeline for a small set of vetted community models; publish pins to internal catalog and expose to Canary Dedicated pool. Phase 2: Broader onboarding with rate-limited public publishing and auto-notify model-owners. Phase 3: Open ingestion for community contributions with manual quick review step for high-risk licenses/models. In any phase, failed compatibility checks prevent publish; an automated rollback job reverts the last pin and notifies the oncall and model intake owners. Monitoring: dashboard for ingest success rate, conversion failures, and profile vs baseline deltas. Post-mortem cadence for any publish that triggers customer-impacting regressions.
notes: Decision: Use a conversion-first worker separated from profiling to keep long-running profiling out of the critical path and allow fast rejection of obviously incompatible artifacts
Trade-off: Accepting small token-level divergence for quantized variants (int8/4) vs strict bit-exact for fp16; set explicit tolerance bands per model family
Security: Integrate sigstore early to provide non-repudiable provenance for customer audits; will require an ops runbook for key rotation
Compatibility policy: implement a three-state outcome: pass, warn (publish allowed but flagged), fail (blocked). Warnings will require a PM sign-off for high-impact models before making them public
